chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Thal'abah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Mudabbir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in making a mosque on the 'idhrah (raised ground/earth mound)."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to build a mosque on raised ground or earth mounds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of building a mosque on an 'idhrah, a term often interpreted by Shia jurists as a raised earth mound or a place of burial. This ruling underscores the principle that natural elevations or burial grounds do not inherently invalidate the sanctity of the space for congregational prayer, provided the ground itself remains pure. It reflects the practical flexibility in Islamic architecture regarding topographical features, ensuring that community worship is not hindered by minor geographical variations.
